headline: 111 killed as 7.4 magnitude earthquake strikes western Colombia, buildings collapse
summary: A powerful 7.4 magnitude earthquake has devastated western Colombia, leaving 111 dead and 87 injured, with rescue efforts underway to free those trapped under rubble across multiple cities.
details: At least 111 people were killed and 87 injured after a powerful 7.4 magnitude earthquake struck western Colombia yesterday. The quake, which hit at a depth of 107km near San Jose del Palmar, caused widespread destruction, knocking down buildings across several cities and trapping many in the rubble.

The disaster immediately presented a major crisis for the new administration, with President Abelardo De La Espriella declaring a national state of emergency. He affirmed that the government has deployed all capabilities to protect lives, assist affected communities, and deliver aid, prioritizing the rescue of those trapped.

The earthquake's impact was felt nationwide, causing a tower of Manizales' beloved cathedral to fall and paralyzing traffic. In Cali, one of Colombia’s largest cities, over two dozen structures collapsed, prompting calls for disaster teams from Bogota and Medellin. Choco Governor Nubia Carolina Cordoba-Curi reported significant damage and injuries in Quibdo, the provincial capital, and issued warnings about potential aftershocks.

headline_marked: [[SSC pass rate hits 19-year low]] at 64.05%, nearly 7 lakh students fail
headline: SSC pass rate hits 19-year low at 64.05%, nearly 7 lakh students fail
summary: The pass rate for the Secondary School Certificate (SSC) exams has dropped significantly for the second consecutive year, with a notable decrease in GPA-5 achievers.
details: The Secondary School Certificate (SSC) examination pass rate has fallen to 64.05% across nine general education boards, marking the lowest in 19 years. This represents a further decline from last year, with approximately 504,929 students failing to pass.

The number of students achieving a GPA-5 also decreased by nearly 19,000 this year, totaling 106,009 compared to 125,018 last year. Dhaka Education Board led in both pass rate and GPA-5 recipients, while Mymensingh Board had the lowest pass rate.

Analysis of the results highlights student weaknesses in English and Mathematics, which are compulsory subjects. Eight out of nine general education boards, excluding Cumilla, reported pass rates below 80% in English, directly impacting the overall pass rate.

Poor performance in the Humanities division also contributed significantly to the overall decline. With over six lakh candidates, the pass rate in Humanities was considerably lower than in Science and Business Studies, despite its large student population.

Educationists suggest that question patterns, student preparation, and answer script evaluation methods influence results. They emphasize the need to review learning standards, subject-specific teachers, and learning gaps in schools, especially given that over five lakh students failed after nearly a decade of schooling.

Girls continue to outperform boys for the 11th consecutive year, with a pass rate of nearly 68% for girls compared to approximately 60% for boys. Girls also secured more GPA-5s, with over 58,000 compared to approximately 47,000 for boys.

The SSC exams were held from April 21 to May 20. A total of 1,404,539 students participated across the nine general education boards, with 899,610 passing. This year's results show a continuation of a downward trend after a long period of high pass rates, prompting calls for a comprehensive review of the education system.
